record.title: CodeMidas builds coding RL tasks from source code and reports gains on five external benchmarks
record.summary: The authors introduce CodeMidas, a pipeline that derives executable reinforcement-learning tasks from implemented functionality in open-source codebases, constructs execution-grounded tests, and filters environments using execution checks and solution rollouts. They report 5,545 training tasks from 3,185 repositories across 23 languages and 15 technical domains. Training MiMo-V2.5 with GRPO on this dataset reportedly improves all five listed external coding benchmarks relative to the same initial policy and evaluation settings. Examples include DeepSWE pass rate rising from 10.0% to 21.7%, Terminal-Bench v2.1 from 63.7% to 72.2%, and ProgramBench Almost Solved from 4.5 to 21.5. The authors report task-set disjointness from CodeMidas Val and the five external benchmark sets. These are author-reported results for one model/training setup, not an independent reproduction or general scaling law.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_PUBLICATION_EVENT
claims.text: The authors posted arXiv preprint 2609.22068v1 on 2026-09-18.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report constructing 5,545 coding reinforcement-learning training tasks from 3,185 open-source codebases spanning 23 programming languages and 15 technical domains, using source-derived task statements, execution-grounded tests and post-rollout filtering.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Training MiMo-V2.5 with GRPO on CodeMidas reportedly improves all five listed external benchmark scores against the same initial policy and identical evaluation settings; examples include DeepSWE pass rate 10.0% to 21.7%, Terminal-Bench v2.1 63.7% to 72.2%, and ProgramBench Almost Solved 4.5 to 21.5.

claims.label: CLAIMED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The reported training and evaluation results concern one MiMo-V2.5 setup and remain author-reported; the authors state task-set disjointness, but no independent reproduction or data-leakage audit was performed in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: The linked code, dataset, checkpoints and evaluation scripts were not inspected or independently reproduced; reported gains and claimed task-set disjointness remain unverified here.
Generalization beyond one model/checkpoint family and one GRPO configuration has not been established.
Verifier false-positive rates, semantic benchmark contamination and task-generation/compute costs were not independently measured.

brief.importance_rationale: If the paper-reported results transfer, deriving executable coding-RL tasks from existing functionality could broaden and improve the supply of verifiable software-engineering training environments. The reported gains span five public benchmarks, but come from one MiMo-V2.5/GRPO run family and author-defined task construction/filtering; they do not establish a general data-scaling law or cross-model result.
limitations: All results are reported by the paper authors; no code, dataset, checkpoint, independent reproduction or leakage audit was performed in this review.

The reported training effect is for MiMo-V2.5 under one GRPO setup with binary execution reward, batch size 32 and 32 rollouts per task. Transfer to other model families, scales, training algorithms or resource budgets is unknown.

External results use the authors’ benchmark task sets and compare against the same initial policy; ProgramBench Almost Solved is the share of tasks passing at least 95% of tests, while the other listed metrics are pass rates.
The paper reports its training-task set is disjoint from validation and external benchmark task sets, but independent semantic/near-duplicate contamination analysis was not performed here.
Environment construction, verifier quality, filtering cost, RL compute and cost per usable task are not independently measured in this review.
brief.summary: The authors introduce CodeMidas, a pipeline that derives executable reinforcement-learning tasks from implemented functionality in open-source codebases, constructs execution-grounded tests, and filters environments using execution checks and solution rollouts. Training MiMo-V2.5 with GRPO on this dataset reportedly improves all five listed external coding benchmarks relative to the same initial policy and evaluation settings. Examples include DeepSWE pass rate rising from 10.0% to 21.7%, Terminal-Bench v2.1 from 63.7% to 72.2%, and ProgramBench Almost Solved from 4.5 to 21.5. technical.claimed_result: Authors report 5,545 tasks from 3,185 open-source codebases and improved scores on all five external benchmark task sets after MiMo-V2.5 GRPO training. Specific reported changes include DeepSWE 10.0% to 21.7%, Terminal-Bench v2.1 63.7% to 72.2%, and ProgramBench Almost Solved 4.5 to 21.5.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public preprint specifies task generation, execution-grounded verification, post-rollout filtering and a one-model GRPO evaluation; outcome metrics and dataset-disjointness checks are reported by the authors. No independent reproduction was done.
technical.implementation_status: Author-reported training and benchmark evaluation on MiMo-V2.5; no independent deployment, cross-model validation or cost study established.
technical.mechanism: Agents inspect implemented code to formulate behavioral specifications, adapt a codebase environment where the target functionality remains unimplemented, derive tests by executing the original implementation, check test consistency, and filter environments through adversarial rollouts, solution review and observed rollout success. The retained tasks provide executable binary rewards for GRPO training.
technical.regime: 5,545 CodeMidas tasks; MiMo-V2.5 with GRPO, binary verifier reward, batch size 32 and 32 rollouts per task. Evaluation uses the same settings for the initial and RL policies on SWE-bench Pro, DeepSWE v1.1, ProgramBench, RepoZero C2Rust and Terminal-Bench v2.1. CodeMidas Val is 200 separate tasks with three attempts each. Authors report train/validation/external benchmark task-set disjointness. ProgramBench Almost Solved requires passing at least 95% of tests; other benchmark metrics are pass rate.
technical.reproducibility: The preprint provides task-generation, training and evaluation details; the linked artifact and data were not inspected or run in this review. All outcome and disjointness results remain author-reported.
technical.strongest_baseline: The same MiMo-V2.5 initial policy evaluated on the same official task sets and identical evaluation settings; the paper also compares filtered 5,545/1k/3k task pools with an approximately 8,000-task unfiltered pool under the same training configuration.

brief.title: CodeMidas builds coding RL tasks from source code and reports gains on five external benchmarks
brief.why_it_matters: Coding-agent RL depends on task diversity and executable reward signals. CodeMidas reports a way to source both from existing software functionality, then filter candidate environments for execution consistency and reward reliability. Its reported benchmark gains make this a meaningful training-data and environment-construction result, while the evidence remains limited to one model/checkpoint family and author-reported filtering/evaluation.
